player.//: Movement (src/sim/player/player.ts). A sprint's force-velocity profile: propulsion accel (m/s^2, F0 per kg) from a standstill, falling linearly with speed to zero at fvSpeed (v0, the profile's intercept, forward; scaled by the direction's top speed over maxSpeed sideways and back), and the run capped at the top speed for the direction run relative to where the player looks (the ball): maxSpeed forward, sideSpeed sideways (crossover steps, head turned), backSpeed backpedalling. F0 8.5 N/kg is the profile's from-rest push for men in court and field sports (8-9, Haugen et al. 2019). The intercept is fitted to the one padel sprint number that doesn't hang on how the clock was started, the 5-10 m split: highly trained padel players 0.85-0.89 s (Saez de Villarreal et al. 2023; their SP5/SP10 don't say what started the clock, and that alone moves times 0.2-0.7 s, Haugen et al. 2012). v0 6.5 gives 0.858 s here (the run reaches the 6 m/s cap just before 10 m); the field-sport v0 of 7.5-11 m/s (Haugen 2019, sprinters' profiles over 30-40 m) reaches the cap by 4 m and gives 0.833 s, faster than padel players are, and with the intercept at the cap (before 2026-10-28) the push faded too early (at 4 m/s 2.8 m/s^2; now 3.3). brake: hardest deceleration; grip: all horizontal acceleration (braking, turning, pushing) together, the shoe on sand-filled turf (mu about 0.9). Match data (Miralles et al. 2025, 83 WPT men, WIMU Pro GNSS + LPS): top speed in a match median 15.2 km/h (4.2 m/s), peak acceleration 4.6 and deceleration -4.5 m/s^2 (tracker-smoothed), about 395 accelerations an hour, 80% of them over 1-2 m. Those tracker peaks are sub-maximal (smoothed, and players rarely go flat out); the body can do more: 5 m forward takes 1.53 s here from a standstill (the force build-up of //split included) and 1.41 s off a split-step, 10 m 2.38 / 2.27 s. The AI uses full effort only when the time left asks for it. sideSpeed, backSpeed and grip are estimates (no published padel figures).
player.//split: Split-step and getting going (FEEL.md, DECISIONS.md Phase 2). Players hop as the opponent strikes: take-off about at their contact, landing 152 ms after it, airborne about 142 ms (world-class tennis, Mecheri et al. 2019); in the air there is no grip. From a static stance force takes time to build: push starts at startFrom of full and reaches it over startRamp; a split-step landing pre-loads the legs (for splitPreload after landing, tuning), so the first step needs no build-up. Calibrated so the split-step reaches a target 1-2.5 m away about 110 ms (11-16% at 1-2.5 m) sooner, as measured (Uzu et al. 2009: 764 vs 868 ms; Nieminen et al. 2014: 13.1%), and with a 170 ms decision the push starts 175 ms after the opponent's contact and the feet have moved 5 cm by 283 ms (tennis, first foot movement: 266-311 ms). splitStepTime is the whole move for the avatar (hop and landing).
player.//reach: Where a ground stroke is met relative to the body's centre: contactFront in front of it (Sanchez-Alcaraz et al. 2021, contact point from the centre of gravity, highly trained players: drive 0.64 +- 0.32 m, lob 0.65 +- 0.32, serve 0.52, volley 0.38, smash 0.45, bandeja -0.01; the game met drives level with the body, 0.00 on average) and reachComfort away from it across the floor (so about 0.67 m out to the side: a drive's contact with the arm nearly straight, the racket's centre about 1 m from the shoulder). Volleys are met volleyFront (0.35 m) in front and volleyReach away (about 0.6 m out: Sanchez-Alcaraz 0.38 m in front; tennis volleys 0.45-0.70 m out by width, docs/research/serve-and-strokes-motion.md 4.2); overheads overheadReach.
player.//reachHigh: How far out a high ball can be reached (review round 2 #7: the reach had been 1.35 m across the floor at any height, so the AI smashed balls 1.0-1.2 m in front of it at 2.5-2.7 m and the racket missed them by up to a metre). Above the shoulder the racket's reach is a sphere about the shoulder: reachArm from the shoulder joint to the face's centre with the arm straight up (standing reach to the face's centre about 2.55 m at 1.80 m: fingertips 1.33 of stature, Drillis & Contini 1966, less the hand, plus the racket's 0.25-0.3 m to the face's centre; so 2.55 - 1.47 = 1.08 m, the shoulder rising a little as the arm goes up), the shoulder raised reachJump by a small jump (smash jumps; contactMaxHeight 2.75 is that reach and that jump), and reachLean for the shoulder's offset from the body's centre and the lean towards the ball. So 1.35 m out up to 1.9 m, 1.10 m at 2.35, 0.87 m at 2.55, 0.3 m at 2.75.
player.//overheadIdeal: Where each overhead is met when the player picks it in advance (the AI; the human's cue keeps overheadIdealHeight, a ring that moved as Space went down mid-charge would play worse): bandeja 1.85-2.05 m (head height or a little above, arm not fully straight), víbora 1.55-1.85 m (shoulder to head height), smash 2.30-2.50 m (full reach, in the air); docs/research/serve-and-strokes-motion.md 4.2. All overheads had been planned at 2.35 m: bandejas too high, smashes at the bottom of their band.
player.//overheadFront: How far in front of the body's centre each overhead is met when it is planned (the stand spot is that far behind the ball, away from the net): Sanchez-Alcaraz et al. 2021 measured the bandeja at -0.01 m (level with the centre of gravity) and the smash at 0.45 m in front; the víbora's side-on contact is put between them. Every overhead had been planned 0.3 m in front: a bandeja's stand spot 0.3 m deeper than it needs, the step that left deep lobs just out of reach (REVIEW.md round 2 #2). overheadFrontAny is the first read before the kind is picked, and a human's plan.
player.//riseMaxOffWall: Off a wall the ball is met at or below the shoulders, or coming down: a ball still climbing past the shoulders after the glass can't be swung at (a ground stroke tops out at the shoulder, and an overhead needs the player under a ball that is falling). Shoulder height 0.818 of stature (Drillis & Contini 1966: 1.47 m at 1.80 m). Without it the AI took 13-15 m/s smash rebounds 0.15-0.3 s after the glass at 2-2.9 m, rising, often with a smash of its own, and only 11% of smashes won (pros 45%).

timing.//: Half-widths of the grade windows in seconds; scaled by the timing-window setting.
